description: Order-to-cash lifecycle backbone as event-driven microservices (.NET 10 + Next.js + MS-SQL Server + MongoDB + Kafka + NATS). Assessment #8 of the order-to-cash trilogy, and its first REUSE RUN: specs/shared/, the harness, the n8n workflows and the stack-agnostic infra are copied from #7, not rewritten. progress/history.md must yield an honest #7 vs #8 benchmark.

rules.state_machine: pending -> [spec_author] -> spec_ready -> HUMAN APPROVES -> in_progress -> [implementer] -> in_review -> [reviewer] -> done | blocked
rules.shared_spec_is_read_only: a change to specs/shared/ is a spec amendment: explicit, human-gated, back-ported to #7 — never a silent fork
rules.reused_ids: R<n> ids are #7's. Reusing one asserts the .NET realisation satisfies the same requirement.

the initial migrations are amended rather than a widening migration added (human gate ruling) — the Phase 6 migrations have never left this machine and have no dependants

features.note: Corrects an error of the leader's, carried for three phases: the plan justified int columns as 'spec parity', but specs/shared/ specifies only 'integer minor units' and never a width. int was #7's MySQL choice, and #7 needs no narrowing because JS numbers are doubles. Keeping int forced a long->int narrowing at every money boundary that #8 alone would pay for. Same category of false parity as the JSON key-order finding in Phase 5.
